papers.title_en: Decoding Naturalistic Speech from fMRI with Temporal Modeling and Multimodal Alignment
papers.authors: Corentin Caris, Louis Jalouzot, Nona Rajabi, Géraud Ilinca, Ahmed Hassayoune, Asilbek Muminov, Thaddée Delebarre, Clara Fonteneau, Charles Maussion, Bertrand Thirion, Alexis Thual, Antoine Collas
papers.tldr: 针对fMRI解码自然语音中噪声和时间模糊挑战，本文提出NOEMA时序卷积解码器，对齐连续fMRI窗口与文本、音频、语音多模态嵌入，直接检索刺激片段。在两个数据集上，2000候选前10命中率超42%，显著优于基线，证实时序建模与多模态对齐的关键作用。
papers.abstract_en: Reconstructing what a person perceives from their brain activity is a stringent test of whether neural recordings carry meaningful information. Naturalistic speech offers a rich testbed for this challenge: it unfolds over multiple timescales, but fMRI's noisy, temporally smeared measurements make this structure hard to recover. We introduce NOEMA, a temporal convolutional decoder that aligns windows of consecutive fMRI measurements with multimodal stimulus embeddings. These embeddings combine complementary text, audio, and speech representations of the same stimulus segment, enabling its retrieval directly from brain activity. On two naturalistic speech datasets, Cephalonauts One and LeBel, NOEMA retrieves the correct segment among 2,000 candidates within the top 10 for more than 42% of held-out queries. This substantially outperforms baseline decoders, an advantage that persists when the candidate pool is extended with thousands of distractors absent from training. Controlled ablations establish the contributions of temporal modeling and complementary stimulus representations.

papers.title_en: Mutual Information in High-Dimensional Neural Coding
papers.authors: Zimo Li, Yuchang Tian, Matthew P. Leighton, Christopher W. Lynn
papers.evidence: 估计互信息以揭示神经群体如何编码刺激
papers.tldr: 针对大神经群体互信息估计面临响应模式指数爆炸的难题，本文提出蒙特卡洛框架，通过从条件独立群体模型采样进行估计。该方法准确恢复基准、校正有限数据偏差，并成功应用于100至10000个神经元的视觉皮层、海马体和视网膜记录，揭示刺激不确定性随群体大小指数衰减的缩放定律。
papers.abstract_en: Estimating mutual information in large neural populations is limited by the exponential growth of possible neural response patterns. Here we apply a Monte Carlo framework to make this problem tractable by sampling from a conditionally independent population model fit from single-neuron responses. The estimator accurately recovers analytical ground truth, corrects finite-data bias, and scales to empirical recordings containing 100 to 10,000 neurons from visual cortex, hippocampus, and retina. Across systems, stimulus uncertainty decays exponentially with population size, revealing a simple scaling law for high-dimensional neural codes.

papers.title_en: An FPGA-Based Spiking Neural Network for Spatiotemporal Pattern Learning and Classification
papers.authors: Jingang Jin, Yue Ma, Zhenhang Zhang, Qinru Qiu
papers.evidence: 用于时空模式分类的脉冲神经网络可作为时序解码算法
papers.tldr: 针对边缘端脉冲神经网络（SNN）部署与在线训练需求，提出一种 FPGA 上推理与训练一体的多层 SNN 实现。采用时间前向训练算法避免 BPTT 的内存和延迟开销，混合精度与架构优化提升资源效率，并解决共享内存的端口冲突和读写依赖。在 MNIST 和五个时间序列数据集上，完全片上训练准确率与 BPTT 相当，吞吐量比 CPU/GPU 高 2.5-6 倍，能耗低一个数量级。
papers.abstract_en: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) are promising for energy-efficient spatiotemporal pattern recognition at the edge, but efficient deployment and on-device adaptation require specialized hardware. In this work, we present an FPGA implementation of multilayer SNNs for spatiotemporal pattern classification, in which both inference and training take place on the same hardware. Our design adopts a temporal-forward-only training algorithm that avoids the memory and latency overhead associated with traditional Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT). A mixed-precision scheme balances training stability with resource efficiency, and architectural optimization maximizes hardware and memory utilization. We further identify and resolve hazards that arise when inference and learning share the same memory, including port conflicts between the forward and backward access patterns and read-after-write dependencies in floating-point potential accumulation. Experimental evaluations on MNIST and five multivariate time-series classification datasets demonstrate that, with fully on-chip training, our SNN model achieves accuracy comparable to SNN or LSTM trained with BPTT. Compared to CPU and GPU based implementations, our FPGA design delivers 2.5 to 6 times higher throughput while consuming an order of magnitude less energy per sample.

papers.title_en: ChronoSheaf: Joint Spatio-Temporal Spectral Filtering on Cellular Sheaves
papers.evidence: 图上的联合时空谱滤波可应用于时序神经信号
papers.tldr: 现有层神经网络将层拉普拉斯视为瞬时空间算子，无法显式建模信号随时间的演化。本文提出ChronoSheaf，引入联合时空的谱层拉普拉斯，并通过过渡限制图（TRM）和双谱滤波器（DSF）在不扩大层结构的情况下扩展时空感受野。在多个时空预测基准上超越最先进方法，验证了联合时空谱滤波的有效性。
papers.abstract_en: Sheaf neural networks generalize graph neural networks by assigning each edge a learned linear restriction map that specifies how the local representations of adjacent nodes relate to one another, thereby mitigating oversmoothing. Existing sheaf architectures, however, define the sheaf Laplacian as an instantaneous spatial operator and therefore cannot explicitly model how signals evolve over time on a graph. We first introduce a spectral sheaf Laplacian, defined jointly over space and time, such that a single operator regulates signal propagation across both the spatial graph and the temporal domain. Directly extending this operator's receptive field in space or time would require increasingly complex sheaf structures. Instead, we propose a spectral filter that expands the effective receptive field along both dimensions without enlarging the underlying sheaf. Building on this operator, we introduce ChronoSheaf, a spatio-temporal sheaf network with two key components. First, Transitional Restriction Maps (TRM) decompose each node's restriction map into a spatial term and two temporal frames that independently control its relation to neighboring nodes at the preceding and following timestep, enabling asymmetric temporal influence. Second, the Dual Spectral Filter (DSF) applies a single bounded-degree polynomial filter with an adaptively estimated spectral radius to the joint spatio-temporal sheaf operator. We validate ChronoSheaf on a diverse set of spatio-temporal forecasting benchmarks, where it outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/ChronoSheaf-1D7D/.
